characters.name: Peter Christen Asbjørnsen
characters.description: Peter Christen Asbjørnsen is depicted as a middle-aged man with a stately presence reflecting intelligence and curiosity. He has a medium build and features a refined appearance marked by keen eyes and a thoughtful expression. His attire is typical of 19th-century Norwegian intellectuals, consisting of a tailored suit and a waistcoat. Asbjørnsen is often seen holding a book or a quill, symbolizing his role as a collector and editor of folklore. His demeanor is serious yet approachable, suggesting a passion for literature and scholarship.

characters.name: Jørgen Moe
characters.description: Jørgen Moe is presented as a distinguished companion to Asbjørnsen, sharing a similar middle-aged stature, albeit with a hint of youthful enthusiasm always present in his eyes. His features are sharp yet gentle, balanced by a kindly smile beneath a well-maintained beard. Moe's clothing mirrors that of scholarly circles—clean, formal, and somewhat subdued, yet indicative of a man of cultural substance. His demeanor is marked by warmth and thoughtfulness, portraying a man deeply engaged with the cultural heritage of his nation.

characters.name: Jacob Grimm
characters.description: Jacob Grimm is characterized as an elder statesman of folklore, with a mature and scholarly appearance. His features are strong and his eyes gleam with a wisdom accrued over years of study. His attire is typical of a learned person from the 19th century, with a richly detailed suit that hints at his German heritage. Grimm's demeanor is stoic, though not unfriendly, exuding a sense of purpose and dedication to the preservation of fairytales and folklore. He is often seen with a thick book, underscoring his role as a foundational figure in the field.

characters.name: Wilhelm Grimm
characters.description: Wilhelm Grimm complements his brother Jacob both in demeanor and appearance, though he carries a slightly more introspective expression. His features are softer, lending an air of gentility to his persona, and he is often depicted with spectacles perched upon his nose, suggestive of his literary efforts. Wilhelm's clothing is refined, echoing the tastes of 19th-century academia. His demeanor is gentle, with an aura of creativity and narrative imagination that reflects his contributions to the realm of folklore and literature.
